rationale: Reviewed 4c46cf64e873b1c6a34ae7688da2737cc7365994, the full BRIEF, G3's round-2 verdict, the round-2 consolidation, spec.md, ADR-0045 and the relevant implementation. The prior destination-policy ask is addressed and the ordinary A-then-A+B fingerprint defect is fixed in the contract. Four gaps remain. Most seriously, the new reachable scan can group an empty sibling merge with a real, reverted landing and thereby PASS MF-3 and let reattest write a binding for reverted work. The line-only MF-4 identity also permits new independent blockers to inherit an old override. Selection and recovery have additional consistency defects. Four scratch probes and fifteen selected baseline safeguards passed. The R4 probe emulates only the specified new candidate generator through the existing scanner seam; the R6 probes model the written, unshipped record/coverage rules, rather than claim implementation exists. The source repository was not modified.
concrete_changes_required: Fix R4.2's same-second-parent fallback grouping/content anchor before approval. Independent sibling merges are not necessarily a linear re-merge chain, and the last merge in topo order must not become an empty anchor that masks the revert of a non-empty landing. Define a fail-closed policy for incomparable anchors (for example refuse the cross-branch ambiguity or check the relevant content-introducing anchors). Extend AC-11 with the exact empty-sibling/real-reverted-landing fixture in repo/internal/lifecycle/g3_round3_probe_test.go: both automatic identification and reattest must refuse, and reattest must write nothing. Preserve the existing linear re-merge/reapply safeguards.

Make R6.2's MF-4 records distinguish independently scoped occurrences with identical line text, retaining multiplicity and enough source/context identity instead of deduplicating solely by kind and line hash. Extend AC-16 with an override for a standalone TBD in the bd description followed by a second standalone TBD in the plan's different design section; ready-check must refuse until fresh evidence is recorded. Pin the analogous repeated checklist-item boundary.

Reconcile R6.4's re-claim recovery with R6.1/R6.2: after release, the fresh next invocation must name ALL currently failing signals, including signals covered by the old marker, because that marker is neither claim authority nor unioned into the replacement. Add a recovery-path AC where MF-3 remains covered and MF-4 becomes uncovered, then invoke release and the recommended fresh claim with MF-3,MF-4 and evidence.

Remove or constrain R1.1's parent-E shortcut so scoped selection agrees with the unchanged FindEpicForBead resolver on conflicting epic dependencies; price the additional reads if needed. Add AC-1/AC-6 coverage for ready E.1 with parent E and a closed blocking dependency on epic E2 returned first by bd show. It must be excluded/named before scoped selection and emit-only, rather than selected and then refused by R1.8. Keep the fail-closed claim guard and pick parity.

findings.title: Round-2 ask status
findings.detail: G3r2.1 ADDRESSED: R4.2:305-321 now admits the short subject as explicitly undirected, requires exact tip/binding confirmation on fallback, and resolves different-second-parent groups only with one corroborated group and no contradictory datum. The ADR-0041 amendment matches this bounded policy. AC-11(viii)/(ix) pin both requested historical shapes, in identification and reattest. The empty sibling content-anchor defect below is NEW_ISSUE, not the former destination-free ambiguity. G3r2.2 PARTIAL: R6.2:398-407 prices Signal.Failures, complete aggregation and a shared raw-record fingerprint; AC-16 pins MF-3 A then A+B, a second MF-4 blocker, determinism and writer/reader agreement. This closes the original first-Detail masking examples, but independently scoped identical-line blockers still collapse to the same identity.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: an empty sibling merge masks a genuinely reverted landing
findings.detail: R4.2:316-320 admits short-form sibling merges and retains same-second-parent grouping with one oldest-anchored content check. Real-git probe TestG3R3EmptySiblingAnchorMasksRealRevert creates X at B; Y independently has the same file, merges X with exact subject 'Merge bead/bead-x' (empty delta), then deletes the file. Separately X genuinely lands on spec/S at M, and git revert -m 1 M removes its content. Y refreshes from that spec history; the spec reaches a main carrier so both X merges are off first-parent. Actual git log --merges --topo-order orders M then the empty sibling E; both have second parent B and X's surviving tip is B. Emulating ONLY the proposed scanner at firstParentMergesFn makes the unchanged checks identify M despite x.txt being absent: the selected oldest anchor E has no delta. Reattest also records M's binding (write seam captured; no real bd write). Control with M alone refuses 'reverted or cleanly removed'. No panel, forged binding, custom ownership subject or commit-tree forge is needed. Probe: repo/internal/lifecycle/g3_round3_probe_test.go; output: probe-results.txt.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: duplicate MF-4 line identities widen override coverage
findings.detail: R6.2:403-405 specifies <kind>:<sha256 of normalised line>, then deduplicates records. TestG3R3DuplicateBlockerFingerprintCollision starts with '### API design\nTBD' in the bd description and later adds '### Security design\nTBD' in the plan section. The actual current MF-4 detector independently confirms both planted blockers. Even a complete all-item aggregator generates the same record twice; sorting/deduplication gives exactly the old fingerprint d708c13bd0e267351eedda490cd704d89796c1019a92f2f2dce99fddcf8bc98e. R6.4's written iff rule therefore still covers the newly blocked security decision, contradicting its promise that one blocker does not cover a second. This is loss of item identity, not a SHA collision. Probe: repo/internal/validate/readiness/g3_round3_probe_test.go.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: ready-check's fresh-claim recovery omits still-failing covered signals
findings.detail: R6.4:433-435 emits release followed by next --allow-not-ready=<uncovered ids>. With MF-3 still failing but covered and a new uncovered MF-4, it emits only MF-4. R6.1:386 requires the full currently failing set to be a subset of the newly named set, and R6.2:410-411 expressly disallows old-marker reuse or union. Consequently the prescribed fresh claim must refuse MF-3. TestG3R3UncoveredOnlyRecoveryCannotReclaim models these exact set rules. This fails closed, but the advertised recovery does not recover and can remove the worktree before the user encounters the avoidable second refusal.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: parent shortcut selects a bead its actual lineage makes unclaimable
findings.detail: R1.1:211 accepts parent==E without consulting FindEpicForBead and R1.8:269 says its checks hold by construction. The unchanged resolver instead iterates all epic dependencies in bd order without checking dependency_type (derive.go:979 onward). TestG3R3ParentShortcutConflictingEpicDependency supplies open pr-aaa.1 with parent pr-aaa and a closed blocks dependency on pr-bbb before its parent-child edge. The actual resolver returns pr-bbb/130-beta. The written R1.1 predicate nevertheless selects it for pr-aaa/129-alpha, including scoped emit-only; R1.8 then safely refuses its claim because pr-aaa.1 is not a plan ID of pr-bbb. Thus no cross-spec mutation is authorized, but selection and claimability disagree despite the central one-predicate promise. A closed prerequisite epic makes this compatible with a bd-ready row. Probe: repo/internal/phase/g3_round3_probe_test.go.

findings.title: Retained trust boundary and verification
findings.detail: The revised contract prevents a stale/abandoned/forged panel registration alone from confirming any fallback candidate and preserves exact surviving-tip/binding contradictions. The primary panel leg remains an unauthenticated exact corroboration under the explicitly accepted ADR-0037 boundary; I am not requesting authentication or a new latest-panel veto. Fifteen selected existing tests passed for spoofed subjects, ancestor-only panels, forged/other-bead/anonymous bindings, inconsistent binding pairs, ambiguity, reverts/reapply, oldest-anchored masked reverts and audited binding repair. These baseline tests do not execute the unimplemented new panel-set reader. Final probe output is in probe-results.txt. Scratch-clone 'go run ./cmd/mindspec validate spec 129-readiness-tracker-honesty' exited 0 with one WARN: lifecycle-binding, spec has no beads epic; no structural error. The initial go-run attempt hit the default Go-cache permission boundary; rerunning with scratch GOCACHE succeeded.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: Non-blocking briefing hygiene: Summary still directs git show 7a490064 instead of the reviewed 4c46cf64; Acceptance criteria says 18 ACs but the artifact has AC-1 through AC-19; the O3 lens still describes epic descendants union metadata.spec_id, superseded by the plan-ID/lineage rule; Round 2's 95-ask arithmetic gives only 91 fixed + 2 refuted + 0 deferred = 93. The suggested source-backed worktree command would also change the read-only source's git administration, so I followed the direct scratch-clone instruction. No TODO(skill) placeholder is present, but the CURRENT Round-3 text itself contains the word TODO on line 86, so its literal claim that the displayed grep matches only the two machine markers is no longer true. The header's beside-BRIEF destination is explicitly overridden; this verdict is written only to the requested scratch/verdict.json.
